newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK 96/97 Govt land earnings seen record HK$60 bln.
newsitem.headline: HK 96/97 Govt land earnings seen record HK$60 bln.

text.p: A surge in the property market has prompted the Hong Kong government to forecast record earnings from land premiums of HK$59.8 billion in 1996/97, Secretary for the Treasury K.C. Kwong said on Thursday.
The figure would exceed expectations by about 40 percent, Kwong said. They compare with HK$45.48 billion earned from land sales, premia and treaty grants in 1995/96 (April/March).
It is likely to boost the government's budget surplus for the year. Accountants and financial analysts have forecast a surplus of as high as HK$25 billion.
Financial Secretary Donald Tsang is scheduled to give his budget speech for 1997/98 next Wednesday.
The budget will cover the period in which Hong Kong reverts to China.
More than 150 years of British rule ends at midnight on June 30, 1997.
"The main reason for the much higher revised estimate in 1996/97 is the buoyancy of the property market," Kwong told a news conference.
The land reveue estimate for 1997/98 is sharply lower, at HK$34.48 billion, which Kwong said reflected the government's policy of assuming steady sales of land.
"It is not really realistic to try to compare land revenue between two consecutive years," he said.

"Land revenue is a capital revenue, it depends very much on the size, location, property market situation et cetera, and therefore even if you are selling about the same amount of land in a year compared to the year before you might get very different premia as a result," he added.

Government spending has not increased as a result of the strong property revenue to comply with Hong Kong's policy of restraining spending below a forecast trend growth rate of the economy, which is pegged at five percent.
"There is a common misunderstanding that if we get more in revenue we can spend more," Kwong said. "That is not how we control expenditure formulation in our budget."
